    Global auxiliary and exact local BGRS Figure 14 quotients #

    In the primitive-projective (opposite) convention, the Figure-14 relation ideal is generated by

    • sigma ≫ alpha₁, represented by P.tau.asHom ≫ first, and
    • alphaₙ ≫ rho, represented by last ≫ Q.tau.asHom.

    The six source vertices deliberately have repeated ambient images. The two central cycles are lambda ≫ delta = sigma and delta ≫ lambda = rho.

    The first construction below forms the same two-generator ideal in all of A. This stronger global quotient is useful for robust cycle-survival estimates, but BGRS 4.3(b) takes the quotient only after restricting to the full corner on the four displayed primitive vertices. The selected-corner construction at the end of the file is the source-exact quotient.

                The unique length-three Figure-14 path survives even in the stronger global auxiliary quotient. In its rightInner-to-leftInner corner, every contribution from the initial relation is a right-radical multiple of the threefold path. Every contribution from the terminal relation is first a left-radical multiple; transit across the nonzero threefold path moves this to another right-radical multiple. Membership would therefore fix the path under a nilpotent endomorphism.
